newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia debt maintain rate cut hopes pre-data.
newsitem.headline: Australia debt maintain rate cut hopes pre-data.

text.p: *The Australian bond market closed firm ahead of Thursday's labour force data amid a feeling that even a very strong rebound in employment will not dent interest rate cut expectations.

The Australian bond market closed firm ahead of Thursday's labour force data, amid a feeling that even a very strong employment rebound will not dent expectations for another official interest rate cut.

Trading remained slow ahead of the report, but the September 10-year bond futures contract struck a fresh 3-1/2 year high of 93.280 at one stage, taking the benchmark October 2007 bond yield below 6.75 percent.
Median expectations centre on a 40,250 employment rise for June, which would all but wipe up the 40,300 slump in May, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
However, it would need an extremely strong rebound to make any impression on unemployment, which is seen only a tad lower at 8.7 percent against 8.8 percent in May.

"Even if you were to get 100,000 (employment rise), the average employment growth in the first six months in 1997 would be only 14,000," said UBS Australia chief economist Stephen Roberts. "That's under what the government wants in its very modest 2-1/4 percent employment growth," he added.
The market maintained a bid bias throughout the session, partly as a hangover to Tuesday's comments by Prime Minister John Howard saying he wanted lower interest rates.

Bullish hopes on interest rates saw September bill futures touch 94.92 at one stage, close to a contract high, and more or less pricing in a 50 basis point easing in current 5.5 percent official interest rates.
The market's firm tone saw it outperform the dollar bloc and the 10-year spread to the U.S. narrow below under 50 basis points and to levels not seen since the early 1980's.
Some analysts are expecting an even further sharp contraction with the U.S. clearly at a different stage of the cycle and the Federal Reserve on a tightening bias.

The local market also outperformed Canada, which succumbed to a mild correction on Tuesday after its recent strong rally. New Zealand debt was under pressure following comments by Treasurer Winston Peters that he saw further weakness in the new Zealand dollar.
